tasks.short: Select and obtain psychology teaching materials

steps.what: Select textbooks and supplies for the psychology course
Request the chosen materials through the existing purchasing process
Check that received materials match the selection and teaching needs

tasks.design: Keep academic selection and receipt checking with the teacher. Use current {PROCUREMENT} requisitions; the proposed scope adds no separate copying or ordering automation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selecting the correct edition and suitable explanations requires academic review.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing purchasing forms already support requesting selected items.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing conceptual accuracy, accessibility, affordability, and course fit.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher recognises when a textbook is unsuitable despite a matching catalogue description.
tasks.altitude: Academic selection and purchasing responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Edition control and library licensing options

evidence.claim: Textbook selection and receipt checking require academic judgement; no additional saving is assumed from an existing requisition process.

assumptions: Boundary is the teacher's selection, requisition, and acceptance effort. Purchasing staff ordering and supplier fulfilment are existing separate work and receive no savings here.

Teacher enters selected item, edition, quantity, course, and budget in s2; that capture remains fully counted. Purchasing staff place the existing order and the supplier delivers after s2 and before s3; delivered materials are not assumed available earlier.
Native purchasing forms remain the first choice; no new structured feed or custom code is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep follows from retaining the existing process.
research_questions: Is any repeated teacher entry present beyond the existing native requisition?

incremental.description: No additional system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net saving zero. Academic selection, existing requisition entry, and receipt checks remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Supervise laboratory work, correct technique, and intervene when needed

tasks.design: Retain direct laboratory supervision and immediate intervention. Existing instructions in {DOCS} may support the session, but their presence does not reduce supervision time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Live student conduct cannot be reliably reconstructed from a completion record.
tasks.enabler_now: No replacement for teacher observation is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Noticing misunderstood procedures and responding to unexpected behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher adapts guidance to what students are actually doing.
tasks.altitude: The teacher remains present and responsible for laboratory supervision.

reach.task: Recognise setup issues affecting a student exercise

evidence.claim: Direct laboratory supervision remains human; no measured replacement or labour saving is supported here.

assumptions: Boundary covers teacher supervision, excluding student labour, laboratory setup by other staff, and separately assessed grading.
Teacher observes student work during the session. Existing laboratory protocols are supplied by the course team; no new structured observation feed is introduced.
Existing native document access suffices; no system change or additional upkeep is proposed.
research_questions: Which observed difficulties require immediate teacher intervention?

incremental.description: No new system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving zero because direct supervision remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review practicum cases and assess the student's clinical reasoning
Supervise clinical work and agree corrective learning or escalation actions

tasks.design: Keep case review and clinical supervision with the qualified teacher. Authorised material in {DOCS} supports the discussion without delegating clinical interpretation or assessment of the student's competence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision requires understanding both client risk and the trainee's reasoning.
tasks.enabler_now: No automated clinical interpretation is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting a trainee's blind spots and recognising when a case exceeds their competence.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor challenges reasoning, observes uncertainty, and accepts professional responsibility.
tasks.altitude: Clinical supervision rights and responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain a supervision concern affecting placement support

evidence.claim: Clinical practicum supervision requires contextual professional judgement; no automation saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary covers teacher supervision, not the student's clinical care or the placement provider's operational duties.

The practicum student and placement supervisor produce existing authorised case material before s1; its preparation remains their unchanged work. No new extraction, model upload, or structured capture is required.
Native restricted document access remains sufficient; unchanged practice adds zero upkeep.
research_questions: Does the existing case review reveal the reasoning and uncertainty needed for effective supervision?

incremental.description: No additional system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net saving zero. Substantive case review and supervision remain with the teacher.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess psychological problems and provide psychotherapy

steps.what: Assess the client's psychological problems and agree an appropriate care approach
Conduct psychotherapy and adapt the intervention to the client's response

tasks.design: Retain psychological assessment and psychotherapy with the appropriately qualified clinician. Existing authorised records in {DOCS} can inform care; this design introduces no automated diagnosis, treatment, or simulated therapeutic relationship.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical meaning depends on context, rapport, uncertainty, and the client's response.
tasks.enabler_now: No change to direct clinical services is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising risk and adapting treatment when the initial understanding is incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: The clinician listens, observes, and takes responsibility for care decisions.

reach.task: Recognise when referral or coordinated support is needed
reach.learn: Local referral pathways and professional boundaries

evidence.claim: Direct psychological assessment and psychotherapy are retained as human services; no labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary covers direct clinical services by a teacher who is appropriately qualified; separate clinical record administration is not an invented saving opportunity here.

Clients supply their account and the clinician produces observations and assessment during s1; subsequent client responses arise in s2. Existing authorised history is obtained through the current care process before assessment.
No structured feed, new model service, or custom software is proposed; native record access remains unchanged and zero incremental upkeep applies.
research_questions: What clinical responsibilities and continuity requirements define this teacher's care role?

incremental.description: No new system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving zero. Assessment and psychotherapy remain direct professional work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The psychology teacher retains academic material selection, live supervision, and clinical care responsibilities.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who provides reliable supervision and appropriate clinical care while using existing purchasing tools for teaching materials.
